title: The Contractor Who Rebuilt at His Own Cost
paragraphs: After discovering that a structural component in a recently completed building did not meet the safety standard he had originally promised, despite the discrepancy being unlikely to be discovered during any routine inspection, Bagir faced a decision with significant financial implications.

His business partner argued that the deviation was minor enough to pose negligible practical risk, and that voluntarily disclosing and correcting it would impose substantial unnecessary costs given the low probability of the issue ever being discovered.

Bagir disagreed, insisting that the promised standard represented a commitment to the client's safety regardless of detection probability, and he proceeded to fund the necessary corrections entirely from his own company's profit margin.

This decision significantly reduced his profit on the project, yet Bagir maintained that building genuine trust within his professional reputation required consistently honoring commitments even when convenient shortcuts remained statistically unlikely to ever be discovered or questioned.
